## Findings

I searched `D:\DownLoads\FinalSuspect-FinalSus\FinalSuspect-FinalSus` for how the FinalSuspect mod handles main-menu button animation effects (hover/floating/breathing), MonoBehaviour injection, cleanup, and PassiveButton usage.

### 1. MonoBehaviour injection via ClassInjector
The **only** MonoBehaviour injected via `ClassInjector.RegisterTypeInIl2Cpp<>()` is **`ErrorText`** (in `FinalSuspect/main.cs:79` and `FinalSuspect/Modules/Core/Plugin/ErrorText.cs`). This is **not** a button/breathing effect — it's an on-screen error display. So **they do NOT create a MonoBehaviour component per button**. Button animations are done entirely via Harmony postfix patches on the existing `MainMenuManager`, plus `PassiveButton` mouse-event listeners.

### 2/3. Button hover animation & cleanup — `MainMenuButtonHoverAnimation.cs`
File: `FinalSuspect/Patches/System/MainMenuButtonHoverAnimation.cs` (also mirrored in `FSSource.txt:19046+`).

- **`Start` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.Start`, Priority.Last): finds the `"Main Buttons"` GameObject and iterates `mainButtons.ForEachChild((Action<GameObject>)Init)`.
- **`Init(GameObject obj)`**: skips `"BottomButtonBounds"` and `"Divider"`; if already tracked, returns; records the button's initial position in a static `Dictionary` via `SetButtonStatus(obj, false)`; then grabs `PassiveButton` and adds:
  - `pb.OnMouseOver.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, true))`
  - `pb.OnMouseOut.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, false))`
- **`LateUpdate` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.LateUpdate`): **early-returns if `!GameObject.Find("MainUI")`** — i.e. the effect only animates while the main menu UI exists, so it self-stops on scene change. It also formats the newsButton color per the current style.
- The actual motion: for each tracked active button, hover moves it **right by 0.35** — on hover uses `Vector3.Lerp(pos, targetPos, Time.deltaTime * 2f)`, on unhover uses `Vector3.MoveTowards(...)`.
- **Cleanup/refresh:** `public static void RefreshButtons(GameObject obj)` resets `MainMenu.AllButtons = new Dictionary<...>()` then re-runs `ForEachChild(Init)`. It's called when the menu needs re-building. There is **no OnDestroy/OnDisable** for these effects — cleanup is implicit: the dictionary entries reference destroyed GameObjects (the code even guards `x.Key != null && x.Key.active`), and the `LateUpdate` guard on `MainUI` stops the animation.

### 4. `Time.deltaTime` — yes, in Update/LateUpdate postfixes
Both `MainMenuButtonHoverAnimation.LateUpdate` (`Time.deltaTime * 2f` Lerp/MoveTowards) and `MainMenuManagerPatch.MainMenuManager_LateUpdate` (RightPanel `Vector3.Lerp(..., Time.deltaTime * 3f/2f)` and BackgroundTexture `Time.deltaTime * 1.4f`, `ShowedBak` one-shot) drive animations inside `MainMenuManager.LateUpdate` Harmony postfixes. `ErrorText` (the only injected MonoBehaviour) uses `Update()`/`LateUpdate()` but only to place/fade error text, not buttons.

### 5. Other PassiveButton effect patterns (`MainMenuManagerPatch.cs`)
In `Start_Postfix`, buttons are created by instantiating the existing credits/quit buttons:
- `SimpleButton.SetBase(__instance.quitButton)` caches a base template; `SimpleButton.SetBase` stores it with **`Object.DontDestroyOnLoad(_baseButton)`** so a re-created template survives scene loads (used for the template object, not the live buttons). `Templates/SimpleButton.cs` and `Templates/TMPTemplate.cs` both use `DontDestroyOnLoad` for base templates.
- Custom buttons (Invite/Website/Github/BugReport/Update) set colors on `passiveButton.inactiveSprites`/`activeSprites` `SpriteRenderer.color` and reset `passiveButton.OnClick = new Button.ButtonClickedEvent()` (clearing listeners) before adding their own — this is their pattern for safely re-adding click handlers on a cloned button.
- The update button gets `MainMenuCustomButtons.Add(button)` tracking.

### OnDestroy/OnDisable usage elsewhere
There are `OnDestroy` patches but none for the main-menu buttons: `MeetingHud.OnDestroy` patches (`MeetingButtonPatch.cs:81`, `PhasePatch.cs:38`) destroy text templates; `IntroCutsceneOnDestroyPatch` sets `IntroDestroyed`. None relate to button breath/floating cleanup.

### Breathing/floating effects
I searched `Breath|breath|Floating|Sine|Mathf.Sin|Time.time`. **There is no breathing/sine animation** applied to the main-menu buttons. The only main-menu animation is the **linear Lerp/MoveTowards hover-slide (right by 0.35)** plus the RightPanel slide and BackgroundTexture one-shot lift. There is no `Mathf.Sin`-based floating anywhere in the mod.

## Summary of their complete approach for button effects
- Don't inject per-button MonoBehaviours. Instead **Harmony-postfix `MainMenuManager.Start`** to collect buttons once and attach `PassiveButton.OnMouseOver/OnMouseOut` listeners that just flip a bool in a static dictionary.
- **Harmony-postfix `MainMenuManager.LateUpdate`** to drive the actual motion each frame with `Time.deltaTime` (Lerp for ease-in on hover, MoveTowards for linear reset). Guard with `if (!GameObject.Find("MainUI")) return;` so animation halts when leaving the main menu.
- Reset/re-track via a manual `RefreshButtons()` that rebuilds the static dictionary.
- No per-effect `OnDestroy`/`OnDisable`; cleanup relies on the `MainUI` existence guard plus null/`active` checks on dictionary keys.
- For persistent button *templates* (not live effects), use `Object.DontDestroyOnLoad` on a hidden cached base instance.

## Next steps
If you intended to replicate a *breathing* (sine) effect, note FinalSuspect does not have one on the main menu — you'd need to add `Mathf.Sin`/`Time.time` scaling yourself (e.g., inside the same `MainMenuManager.LateUpdate` postfix or a small `ClassInjector`-registered MonoBehaviour with an `OnDestroy`-based cleanup). The hover-slide pattern above is fully reusable as-is.

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.

File: `FinalSuspect/Patches/System/MainMenuButtonHoverAnimation.cs` (also mirrored in `FSSource.txt:19046+`).

- **`Start` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.Start`, Priority.Last): finds the `"Main Buttons"` GameObject and iterates `mainButtons.ForEachChild((Action<GameObject>)Init)`.

  - `pb.OnMouseOver.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, true))`
  - `pb.OnMouseOut.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, false))`
- **`LateUpdate` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.LateUpdate`): **early-returns if `!GameObject.Find("MainUI")`** — i.e. the effect only animates while the main menu UI exists, so it self-stops on scene change. It also formats the newsButton color per the current style.
- The actual motion: for each tracked active button, hover moves it **right by 0.35** — on hover uses `Vector3.Lerp(pos, targetPos, Time.deltaTime * 2f)`, on unhover uses `Vector3.MoveTowards(...)`.

File: `FinalSuspect/Patches/System/MainMenuButtonHoverAnimation.cs` (also mirrored in `FSSource.txt:19046+`).

- **`Start` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.Start`, Priority.Last): finds the `"Main Buttons"` GameObject and iterates `mainButtons.ForEachChild((Action<GameObject>)Init)`.
- **`Init(GameObject obj)`**: skips `"BottomButtonBounds"` and `"Divider"`; if already tracked, returns; records the button's initial position in a static `Dictionary` via `SetButtonStatus(obj, false)`; then grabs `PassiveButton` and adds:
  - `pb.OnMouseOver.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, true))`
  - `pb.OnMouseOut.AddListener(() => SetButtonStatus(obj, false))`
- **`LateUpdate` postfix** (`MainMenuManager.LateUpdate`): **early-returns if `!GameObject.Find("MainUI")`** — i.e. the effect only animates while the main menu UI exists, so it self-stops on scene change. It also formats the newsButton color per the current style.
- The actual motion: for each tracked active button, hover moves it **right by 0.35** — on hover uses `Vector3.Lerp(pos, targetPos, Time.deltaTime * 2f)`, on unhover uses `Vector3.MoveTowards(...)`.
- **Cleanup/refresh:** `public static void RefreshButtons(GameObject obj)` resets `MainMenu.AllButtons = new Dictionary<...>()` then re-runs `ForEachChild(Init)`. It's called when the menu needs re-building. # Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.

# Instructions for MCP Server 'TJGenerators'
You are an AI generation assistant with 3D model, image, video, and world generation capabilities.

## Uploading Local Files (3-step workflow)

When a user provides a local file path (e.g. /path/to/image.png) and wants to use it as input for any generate_* tool:

1. Call `file_upload` with `file_path` → returns `{ upload_url, file_url, expires_in }`
2. Upload the actual file bytes by running a shell command: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X PUT -T <file_path> "<upload_url>"`. Confirm output is `200`.
3. Use the returned `file_url` (NOT upload_url) as the `image_url` or `image_urls` parameter in generate_image / generate_3d_model / generate_video / generate_skybox / generate_world / generate_sprite_animation / generate_game_ui_kit / generate_sprite_atlas / upscale_image, as the `model_url` parameter in unirig_rig, or as the `audio_url` parameter in voice_clone.

## Generation Tools

- generate_3d_model: text-to-3D or image-to-3D (tripo P1 default, tripo H3.1 for ultra-high detail when explicitly requested, rodin Gen-2.5 for high-quality tiers, hunyuan 3.1 for explicit request or different-model retry)
- generate_image: text-to-image or image-to-image (seedream for fast/simple, seedream_pro for high-quality Seedream, frontier-game-design for highest quality/complex; auto-selected unless seedream_pro is explicitly requested)
- generate_video: text-to-video or image-to-video (Seedance2)
- generate_effect_video: chained VFX workflow — generates image then video (Seedance2) in one task
- generate_world: text-to-world or image-to-world (World Labs Marble)
- generate_sound_effect / generate_music / generate_tts / generate_material: audio & texture generation
- voice_clone: clone a voice from an audio sample, returns custom_voice_id for use with generate_tts voice_id

## Sprite Animation

- generate_sprite_animation: generate a 4×4 grid sprite sheet (16 frames) via frontier-game-design, then cut and assemble into a 2D sequence-frame animation in Unity
- generate_game_ui_kit: two-step async chain — Step 1 generates a game UI screenshot; Step 2 uses it as reference to produce a UI cutout sheet on magenta background for element extraction
- generate_sprite_atlas: pack multiple sprite images into a single atlas texture (synchronous, returns result immediately, no polling)
- upscale_image: AI super-resolution upscaling via Real-ESRGAN (1x-8x, async, poll every 10s)

## Rigging & Motion Tools

- unirig_rig: auto-rig a 3D model (.glb/.fbx/.obj) into rigged FBX with skeleton and skin weights (UniRig)
- generate_motion: generate character animation from text description (HY Motion)

All generate_* tools return a task_id immediately (async). Use check_task with the task_id to poll for completion.
3D generation: 30s-3min. Video: 1-5min. Image: faster. World: 1-5min. Rigging & Motion: 1-3min.
Poll check_task every 40s for 3D/video/world/rigging/motion tasks, every 10s for other tasks, until status is "completed" or "failed".
IMPORTANT: You MUST launch a background subagent (task tool with run_in_background=true) to poll check_task at the recommended interval. Do NOT poll check_task directly in the foreground.
